reader.requirement: A comma or semicolon immediately followed by a space is a separator accepted wherever the separator space may stand (between any two character-strings, in every division, in headers, clauses, statements, lists and compiler-directing COPY/REPLACE text), except that a comma inside a PICTURE character-string is a PICTURE symbol; a comma or semicolon not followed by a space is no separator.
reader.edition-search: grep -i 'edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion' over SeparatorRule.cs (its summary: edition-invariant) and CobolLexer.g4 (only the case-mapping spelling and the reference-paren word set, neither touching ', '/'; '); the separator rules FNARG_SEPARATOR, PIC_WS, SEMICOLON carry no predicate on the edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: lists, subscripts, reference modifiers, qualifiers and the PICTURE boundary; not exercised: division/section headers, ENVIRONMENT and FILE SECTION clauses, level numbers, 88 VALUE THRU, statement keyword pairs (GO, TO; STOP, RUN), COPY ... REPLACING and REPLACE text, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, a separator comma at line end

probes.expected: accepted: ', ' and '; ' in IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, SELECT, ASSIGN, FD, level numbers, PIC, 9(3), VALUE, 88 VALUE, 1, THRU; 3, OCCURS, MOVE, IF/ELSE, ADD GIVING, OPEN, PERFORM, 2, TIMES, GO, TO; STOP, RUN; PIC 9,999 keeps its comma
COPY, CPYA; REPLACING, ==CPY-X==, BY; ==CPY-Y== and REPLACE, ==XX==; BY, ==N== applied; DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA literal 1,5 with 'TO XX, M' separator

probes.printed: COBOL2631 the comma is not immediately followed by a space, so it is not a separator
probes.expected: ADD A,B refused: a comma without a following space is no separator

probes.printed: COBOL2631 the semicolon is not immediately followed by a space

probes.expected: PIC 9,999, VALUE: the inner comma is the PICTURE symbol, the trailing ', ' a separator; a comma ending an area B line is a separator; literals followed by ', ' and '; '

citations.check: OK  §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR2  (4.2.1 Separators)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: The lexer skips ', '/'; ' exactly as a space outside list regions and keeps it only as an item boundary inside one; PIC_WS and OnPictureString keep a comma inside the PICTURE string. The preprocessor treats the separator as a space when matching. No edition switch on the path; the COBOL2631 refusal text cites §2023:8.3.5 at --std 85 (wording only).

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR1-SR9 and the closing paragraph (PICTURE strings delimited only by space, comma, semicolon, period). Probes at --std 85 aimed at what the reader did not try: s1 (PIC, 999; PICTURE IS; X(3), VALUE; PIC 9(3), VALUE, 5; 'MOVE A TO C, .' comma before the period; '...C; .'; FUNCTION MAX (A, W; E (1)) in COMPUTE) -> runs 'A=007, B=AB ; C=007' 'F=007'; s1p (subscript 'E (W, )', comma separator before the right parenthesis, SR8/SR9) -> 'E=5'; s2 (DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA: 'ADD 1, 2 TO X' and 'ADD 1,5; 2 TO Y') -> 'X=003 Y=003,5' (the ', ' after 1 a separator, 1,5 a literal); s3 (comma in column 72 with sequence text in 73-80, line continues 'Q.'; COPY CPYS REPLACING ==X; Y== BY ==Y== against library text 'ADD X, Y TO Z') -> 'Z=2 P=7 Q=7' (column-72 comma a separator; the pseudo-text separators match as spaces); refusal half: s4 'PIC 9(3),VALUE 5' -> COBOL0307 (the comma without space stays in the PICTURE string); s5 'PIC 9;9' -> COBOL0808 invalid PICTURE symbol ';'. A first s1 run with FUNCTION MAX as a DISPLAY operand was refused COBOL0900 (a 1985 operand-position rule, not this one). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR2  (4.2.1 Separators)  the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR9  (4.2.1 Separators)  the text is in SR9'.
